messages:
dave: New hire stuck during onboarding. Followed mac quickstart, brew install redwoodctl, then ran `redwoodctl auth login` which printed "Authenticated" and showed token path. But samples and local serve both report "rpc: unauthenticated". Strange bit: their dotfiles set XDG_CONFIG_HOME in ~/.zshenv, and oh-my-zsh plugin loads before their exports.

rachel: can you paste the exact output of `redwoodctl auth login` and `echo $XDG_CONFIG_HOME`? Also `ls -la $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/redwood` and `ls -la ~/.redwood`?

dave: output: `Authenticated. Token written to /Users/newhire/.config/redwood/token`
$XDG_CONFIG_HOME -> /Users/newhire/.config
ls ~/.config/redwood -> token present
ls ~/.redwood -> directory does not exist
But `redwoodctl samples run` fails unless we export REDWOOD_CONFIG_DIR or create `~/.redwood` symlink.

mina: i've seen a subtle variant: some zsh setups source /etc/profile or plugin scripts early which run the postinstall hook from brew as a login shell, so the installer writes the token into XDG path at install-time, but the runtime binary (when invoked from their interactive shell) has HOME or XDG unset or pointing elsewhere due to early plugin code. Could be shell init ordering causing different resolved config dir at install vs runtime. Did they install via brew as root or via user?

dave: they used brew normal user. I tested locally: if I put `export XDG_CONFIG_HOME=~/.config` in ~/.zshrc it works, but in their setup the export is in ~/.zshenv that runs too late for the installer postinstall step (weird). Also some plugin overrides HOME for sandboxing during shell startup.

jen: two actionable things: 1) on the CLI side, make the binary robust: probe multiple locations (XDG, legacy ~/.redwood, then env override REDWOOD_CONFIG_DIR), and when install-time token is written, also write legacy path for compatibility. 2) add a `redwoodctl doctor` command that prints resolved config dir(s), env vars (XDG_CONFIG_HOME, REDWOOD_CONFIG_DIR), and token discovery order so users can quickly see mismatches.

mina: agree. Also edge case: if both locations exist with different tokens, we need deterministic precedence and a migration helper `redwoodctl migrate-config --from xdg --to legacy` (or vice versa) that safely copies tokens and warns about conflicts. Otherwise users will be confused which profile is active.

dave: quick workaround posted for new hires: `ln -s ~/.config/redwood ~/.redwood` or export `REDWOOD_CONFIG_DIR=$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/redwood` in shell rc. I added the note to onboarding doc.

rachel: opened issue and PR draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwoodctl/issues/1155 "cli: resolve config dir parity and add doctor + migrate-config". Proposed changes in PR: (a) runtime checks XDG then legacy, (b) homebrew formula postinstall writes both, (c) add e2e test matrix with XDG unset/set and plugin-like environment, (d) new CLI `doctor` output.

eng-cli-bot: CI note: changing config discovery will require updates to our CI images and docs that assume `~/.redwood`. Please add compatibility tests and update buildkite scripts. Also consider printing a friendly hint on unauthenticated errors: "If you recently installed, try `redwoodctl doctor` or set REDWOOD_CONFIG_DIR to your XDG path."

jen: i'll pick up the PR to implement probing and doctor. mina, can you add the migrate-config helper spec? Also let's add a debug log at startup that shows the first three config paths checked (but only in --verbose).

mina: will write spec and add tests. I'll also include the case where a samples runner spawns a subprocess — ensure we propagate the resolved REDWOOD_CONFIG_DIR and REDWOOD_ACTIVE_PROFILE in the child env. That was a different flake we fixed earlier.

dave: thanks all. Leaving symlink in place for the new hire until the fix lands. i'll paste repro logs into the GH issue and link this thread. :thumbsup:
